guide: Multi-AZ: no extra charge for standby.
correct: You pay for the standby instance, so Multi-AZ roughly doubles the instance cost. Only the replication traffic inside the region is free.

guide: Standard → Glacier Instant Retrieval needs a 90-day minimum.
correct: The 30-day lifecycle minimum applies only to Standard-IA and One Zone-IA. GIR can be a day-0 transition. The 90 days is GIR's minimum storage-duration charge, a separate rule.

guide: One Zone-IA → Glacier Instant Retrieval in the waterfall.
correct: One Zone-IA cannot transition to GIR. It can only go to Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive.
The default NACL allows all traffic. A custom NACL denies everything until you add rules.
Up to about 66%.
6 categories (Operational Excellence was added). Basic and Developer plans now get more than 7 checks.

topic: Who recommends RIs and Savings Plans
guide: No service picks RI/Spot/SP for you. You decide.
correct: Cost Explorer (and Cost Optimization Hub) recommends which Savings Plans or RIs to buy from your usage. Nothing buys them for you, and Compute Optimizer only right-sizes.
DocumentDB Global Clusters exist and replicate across regions, like Aurora Global Database.
Multi-AZ is supported, with higher IOPS. The exam trigger is still "ZFS migration".
Partition groups can span multiple AZs in a region (up to 7 partitions per AZ). Only Cluster is single-AZ.
Batch can run jobs on Fargate, which is serverless.

guide: Bucket policy can do cross-account, IAM policy can't.
correct: Cross-account needs both: the bucket policy grants the other account, and that account's IAM policy grants its user.

guide: You must create a new bucket with the multi-region key.
correct: No new bucket needed. Switch default encryption to the new multi-region key, then re-encrypt existing objects (copy in place or S3 Batch Operations).
Secrets Manager has native multi-region secret replication.

guide: Athena does NOT support fetching partial content.
correct: Misleading. Athena selects columns and rows, and with Parquet/ORC it reads only the columns it needs.
5 per region (soft limit).

guide: Session Store listed as a caching strategy.
correct: Session store is a use case. The strategies are Lazy Loading, Write-Through and TTL (missing from the guide).

guide: Legal Hold listed as a retention mode.
correct: Two modes: Governance and Compliance. Legal Hold is a separate on/off flag with no expiry. Governance changes need s3:BypassGovernanceRetention.

guide: Point root domain to EC2: you can't use Alias, so put an ALB in front.
correct: A plain A record pointing at the instance's Elastic IP works at the apex. Alias isn't needed, and an ALB is only needed if you want load balancing.

guide: On-demand is 2.5x more expensive per request.
correct: On-demand prices dropped about 50% in Nov 2024 and AWS now recommends it by default. Provisioned wins only for steady, high-utilization traffic.

guide: Use S3 Select to filter data server-side.
correct: Closed to new customers since July 2024. Pick it only if it's the only sensible option.
QLDB reached end of support in July 2025. Newer questions point to Aurora PostgreSQL for ledger-style needs.

guide: Listed as a current Storage Gateway type.
correct: No longer available to new customers since late 2024.
Closed to new customers since July 2024. Older questions may still use it.

guide: CRITICAL exam trap, appears multiple times.
correct: New accounts can't create Launch Configurations (since Oct 2024). Know it's immutable, but don't spend effort on it.
The buffer interval can go down to 0s now. "Near real-time" is still the exam word.
Since 2024 you can create geoproximity records as normal records. Traffic Flow is optional.
IAM Access Analyzer also has unused access findings now. "Last accessed" still points to Access Advisor.
KMS HSMs are now Level 3 validated too. The exam still picks CloudHSM for single-tenant HSMs you control.
Verify: raised to 80,000 IOPS in 2025. Learn 16,000 for the exam. Also: gp2 IOPS are tied to size (3 IOPS/GB), gp3 IOPS are independent.
Verify: raised to 1 MiB in 2025. The exam answer for big payloads is still the SQS Extended Client + S3.
Verify: raised to 50 TB at re:Invent 2025. Learn 5 TB for the exam.
It can now be raised for Regional and Private REST APIs. The exam answer is still 29s.

guide: ACM certs can't be used on EC2.
correct: Verify: exportable public certificates arrived in 2025. The exam answer is still to terminate TLS on ALB or CloudFront.
